answer: An agent marketplace selling tundra surveys, comet forecasts, and meadow maps weights governance votes by tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, rather than by account count. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand fake agents still yields only 100 votes. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, tying up capital for the full period and bearing price risk; creating extra identities alone buys no power.
